newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian sex scandal prompts more abuse revelations.
newsitem.headline: Belgian sex scandal prompts more abuse revelations.

text.p: The success of investigations into Belgium's "Dutroux" scandal of child abduction, sexual abuse and murder has given hundreds of people the courage to finally reveal past sexual abuse.

"It is an absolute explosion. We are being swamped by children and people who are now adults coming forward to tell how they have been sexually abused," Eliane Masson of the support group Marc et Corine told Reuters.
The group specialises in counselling and helping the parents of children who have been abducted. It is named after two children who were kidnapped and killed in the late 1980s.

The unmasking of a paedophile ring allegedly led by convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux has shaken Belgium to the core and prompted hitherto unasked questions about the moral and political health of the country.
Four young girls have been found dead since mid-August -- at least two starved to death. Two others have been rescued.
Police have found the body of an accomplice whom Dutroux admits killing, and are searching for seven other children.
"Hundreds have been coming forward...They are from all over the country as well as France, the Netherlands and even Britain," Masson said.
She stressed that most had no connection with the Dutroux investigations that are being led by investigating magistrate Jean-Marc Connerotte and public prosecutor Michel Bourlet.
"The attitude of Connerotte and Bourlet has given people the courage to come forward," she said.
An example of the new mood in the country was the arrest last week in the eastern, Germanophone town of Eupen of 60-year-old Catholic bishop Gerard Franck on charges of child sex abuse.

The arrest was revealed late on Tuesday. Belgian newspapers said on Wednesday two brothers, now 27 and 23 years old, had been prompted by the Dutroux investigations to come forward and formally complain against Franck.
The two stated that Franck, a member of the Old Catholic Church that split from Rome in 1870, began abusing the older boy when he was 10 and did not stop until he was in his teens.
Eupen public prosecutor Rolf Lennertz said the two came from a very religious family and had been mentally manipulated by Franck.
Police are investigating to see if any other children were involved.
Masson said most of the people coming forward now to reveal recent or long-distant abuse were girls or women.
"They are from both sexes, although the majority we are getting are from young girls," she said.
She added it was clear that the police were also taking such complaints much more seriously than they apparently had in the past.
The Dutroux case has revealed a catalogue of bungling, incompetence and rivalry between different police forces and the judiciary, prompting allegations of possible police complicity.
The arrest late on Monday of gendarme Gerard Vannesse on charges of drug trafficking and car theft -- the other side of the Dutroux case -- has done nothing to dispel the fears.

Vannesse was the 13th person -- and the second policeman -- to be arrested and charged in the case. Seven people, including Dutroux, his second wife Michelle Martin and flamboyant businessman Jean-Michel Nihoul remain in detention.
